smallest_next_extensions.extension: Observe the actual Library/Favorites file-list container, not the entire conversation renderer
smallest_next_extensions.why: The saved runtime reaches depth20 and node800; sidebar/chat content can consume the budget. Scope to a freshly observed collection container and reset relative depth. Keep caps and errors visible; raising whole-page limits does not establish complete collection coverage.
smallest_next_extensions.scope_boundary: Find the collection by observed container/ancestry and selected Favorites state; do not filter individual source files by research keywords or expected filenames.

smallest_next_extensions.extension: Reuse real child enumeration for any future path-based action lookup
smallest_next_extensions.why: Observer paths now distinguish /index:N for object children and /child:actualID for simple children. The retained legacy navigation traversal still uses sequential get_accChild indices and its old /1/2 paths. Do not feed a new observation path into that old resolver. Root can reuse the same AccessibleChildren traversal before adding a file-open operation.
smallest_next_extensions.action_boundary: Validate one fresh renderer/window identity, current container, full name, role, state, location/defaultAction and globally unique observed target. Refuse disabled/offscreen/invisible/stale or ambiguous matches. Existing Library/Favorites names remain navigation controls, not a generic arbitrary-name click API.

smallest_next_extensions.extension: Open one observed file and verify the original-byte route before repeating the same bounded action over all files
smallest_next_extensions.why: A file-row default action may open a preview, while a nearby star/menu action may mutate Favorites. Inspect the actual role, full name and defaultAction before the parent invokes it. Verify the resulting file title/reference/content view, then prefer a native exact-reference or observed Download Original action. A successful single-file route is a transport proof, not a one-file scope reduction.
smallest_next_extensions.action_boundary: No guessed paths, file references or URLs; no clipboard/cookie/session-store extraction; no new authenticated browser or persistent crawler. The parent owns navigation and checks each postcondition.

smallest_next_extensions.extension: Handle virtualized/paginated continuation as an explicit observed read-navigation action
smallest_next_extensions.why: AccessibleChildren enumerates exposed children, not necessarily every source item in a virtualized folder. Keep set counts, next/load-more/scroll availability and observed positions. When authorized, parent performs one bounded observed navigation/scroll action then re-observes, with a finite unchanged-state budget. Missing or clipped items remain a concrete coverage gap.
smallest_next_extensions.completion_boundary: An empty accessibility result under a cap, a disappearance between snapshots, or a zero Pages API result cannot mean the Favorites folder is empty or fully processed.

source_quality_acceptance: Every Favorites occurrence remains in the manifest regardless of filename, extension, apparent relevance or relationship to the20-image subset.

Preserve exact collection/breadcrumb provenance, native item/reference identity where available, displayed name/type/size/date, snapshot provenance and retrieval outcome; do not overwrite duplicate filenames.
Distinguish observed_in_favorites, original_bytes_acquired, content_extracted, unsupported_format and inaccessible. Filenames, preview text and thumbnails are not original bytes.

Hash originals before extraction. Preserve document page/sheet/cell/formula structure and image pixels, dimensions, orientation, diagrams, tables, arrows, colors, axes, overlaps and layer relationships. OCR is a derived text layer, not a substitute for geometry-bearing originals.
Keep ambiguities, native labels, source roles, original user corrections and extraction truncation. Do not invent shapes, operators, orientation locks or unseen text to fill a retrieval gap.

Reconcile observed folder counts and pagination/virtualization with per-item outcomes before claiming all intended sources were collected. A count of exposed accessibility nodes is not a file count or an account-completeness certificate.

official_sources.title: AccessibleChildren — Microsoft Learn
official_sources.supports: The start parameter is a child index; returned variants carry the actual childID or IDispatch. Use returned identities rather than treating an index as a childID.

official_sources.title: How Clients Obtain Child IDs — Microsoft Learn
official_sources.supports: Native enumeration yields childIDs/interface references; returned interface resources have a lifecycle and must not become a persistent unbounded collector.

official_sources.title: Working with Virtualized Items — Microsoft Learn
official_sources.supports: Only realized virtualized items may exist in accessibility trees, and realization can change scrolling; visible inventory alone is insufficient.
